implemented_requirements.requirement: Directional input controls the snake (arrow keys / WASD)
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → handle_keydown maps pygame.K_UP / K_w to self.snake.turn(settings.UP) (and similarly for DOWN, LEFT, RIGHT).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake moves around the board each tick
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → update() accumulates time and calls step(); step() calls self.snake.update() which inserts a new head based on current direction.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Food items appear on free cells and are rendered
implemented_requirements.evidence: food.py → randomize_position() builds free_cells excluding snake body and picks one; draw() renders a rect with settings.COLOR_FOOD.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake grows when it eats food
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → step() checks head == food.position, then self.snake.grow() and re‑randomizes food.
game.py → step() sets game_over if self.snake.check_self_collision() returns True; snake.py → check_self_collision() compares head with body[1:].
game.py → step() sets game_over if self.snake.check_boundary_collision() returns True; snake.py → check_boundary_collision() checks coordinates against GRID_WIDTH/HEIGHT.
game.py → draw() clears screen, draws grid, food, snake, HUD and flips the display each loop.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Current score is shown and updated with food eaten
implemented_requirements.evidence: game.py → step() adds self.score_multiplier to self.score on food eat; ui.draw_score() displays score, high score and difficulty.
settings.py defines DIFFICULTIES with speed and score_multiplier; menu.py lists them; Game.__init__ reads config = settings.DIFFICULTIES[difficulty_name].
game.py → handle_keydown toggles self.paused on key K_p; draw() shows pause overlay via ui.draw_center_message.

critical_issues: None that prevent core gameplay. All major features are present and the code appears runnable.
judge.summary: The provided source files implement a complete, classic Snake game: directional controls, food spawning, growth, self‑ and boundary collision detection, scoring, and selectable difficulty levels. The main loop, rendering, UI helpers, and menu are all present, and no fatal errors are evident, making the solution likely executable and satisfying the benchmark.
